sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Mohammad Saqib, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and Sri Neeraj Kumar Sharma, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the cognizance/summoning order dated 12.04.2022, charge sheet dated 02.03.2022 as well as the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No. 574 of 2022 (State Vs. Chandra Prakash and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 510 of 2021,
under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act against the applicant nos. 1, 2, 3 and 4, and under Sections 498-A, 323, 354, 354-Kh, 354-g, 342, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P.Act against the applicant no.5, Police Station Sikandera-rau, District Hathras,
pending in the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Hathras on the basis of compromise.
3.

sentences.text: It is further stated that pursuant to the order passed by this Court, the parties appeared and the court concerned verified the aforesaid compromise vide order dated 26.05.2023.
Certified copy of the order dated 26.05.2023 is placed on record.

5. Counsel for the applicants submits that if the criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship that is arising between the hitherto bitterly estranged couple and their families.
6. Counsel for the opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the submissions advanced by the counsel for the applicants or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.

7. In view of the fact that the dispute appears to be purely of a personal nature being a matrimonial dispute that has been mutually settled between the parties, to their satisfaction, no useful purpose would be served in allowing such a prosecution to proceed any further.

8. Thus, in view of the well settled principles of law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in B.S.
Joshi v. State of Haryana, 2003(4) SCC 675, as well as Nikhil Merchant v. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, J.T., 2008 (9) SC 192, the proceedings of the aforesaid case are hereby set aside.

sentences.text: 9. It is next contended that earlier the instant matter was referred to the Mediation and Conciliation Center of this Court for settlement.

Pursuant thereto the applicant had deposited a sum of Rs.
18,000/- before the Center.
Out of which Rs. 15,000/- was to be paid to the opposite party no.2.

Since the opposite party no.2 failed to appear before the Mediation Center, hence the amount of Rs.
15,000/- may be returned to the applicants.

sentences.text: Perused the report of the Mediation Centre dated 29.10.2022 and after considering the aforesaid submission, liberty is accorded to the applicant no.1 to file an appropriate application before the Mediation Center for return of Rs. 15,000/- within three weeks from today.
In case the aforesaid application is filed, the Mediation Center is directed to return the amount of Rs. 15,000/- to the applicant no.1 within two weeks thereafter.
11. With the aforesaid direction, the present application is allowed.
